title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din (1137-1193) lived a century after El Cid's exile and campaigned in Egypt/Syria, never in Iberia. The engine offers period-appropriate alternatives or a generic Castle-age enemy commander, so this was avoidable.

37 CAMEL_RIDER units as the core of the Muslim army: taifa and even Almoravid forces in eastern Iberia fought as horse cavalry (jinetes/heavy horse) and infantry; camel cavalry en masse belongs to a North African/Levantine setting, and the engine's Cavalier/Light Cavalry/Cavalry Archer would have served.
18 TREE_PALM_FOREST tiles plus ROMAN_RUINS/TEMPLE_RUIN dressing give a Near-Eastern desert look rather than the Ebro valley and Levantine huerta of Zaragoza and Valencia.

Minaya Alvar Fanez speaks throughout the dialogue but no unit represents him; conversely no representation at all of Alfonso VI, al-Mutamin of Zaragoza, Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona, or al-Qadir/Ibn Jahhaf of Valencia, the actual named parties of 1081-1094.

issues_found: The enemy commander is the SALADIN hero — a Kurdish sultan of Egypt/Syria active c. 1169-1193 in the Levant, with no connection to Iberia. The opponents of El Cid's exile years were al-Mundhir of Lerida/Denia, the Count of Barcelona Berenguer Ramon II, the Almoravids under Yusuf ibn Tashfin, and the Valencian qadi Ibn Jahhaf. Since the engine offers no Iberian-Muslim hero, a renamed generic Camel Rider or Cavalier would have been the correct stand-in; placing a different named historical hero is avoidable error.

Both players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture, unit sets and language are unassigned — Spanish for El Cid's retinue and Saracens (or Berbers) for the taifa/Almoravid side were both available.
37 CAMEL_RIDERs dominate the enemy army; Andalusi and Almoravid forces in eleventh-century Spain fought as light horse (jinetes) and Berber lancers, not massed camelry.
18 TREE_PALM_FOREST tiles give a Saharan/Levantine look rather than the Ebro valley and Levantine huerta around Zaragoza and Valencia.

El Cid's captain Minaya Alvar Fanez appears only in dialogue; the only representation is an unnamed generic KNIGHT whose death triggers defeat — a named or at least distinguished unit was trivially available.

The narrative spine is invented generic questing: a 'deeper plot against Zaragoza's throne', an 'Ambush Leader', a 'Traitor' who reveals himself, a 'Rescued Ally', and a 'Villain Confrontation' with 'Villain Speech'. None of this corresponds to the documented campaigns of 1081-94 (Almenar, Morella, the defeat and capture of Berenguer Ramon II at Tevar, the twenty-month blockade of Valencia).

The 1093-94 siege of Valencia is compressed into a single fortress storm with a duel against the enemy leader; in fact the city fell to a long starvation blockade and negotiated surrender, and the Almoravid relief army withdrew without battle.
Primary victory is the assassination of SALADIN, so the encoded goal rewards killing a man who was never in Spain rather than taking the city.

Player 2's commander is the SALADIN hero — an Ayyubid Kurdish sultan of 12th-century Egypt/Syria, a century later and from an entirely different theatre than the Taifa/Almoravid lords of Zaragoza's rivals or Valencia. The engine offers generic Saracen/Berber units that could have been renamed 'al-Qadir', 'Ibn Jahhaf' or 'Berenguer Ramon II', so this was avoidable.

Both players' civilizations are set to RANDOM, so architecture, unit skins and tech tree may render as Britons, Japanese, Aztecs, etc.; Spanish for El Cid and Saracens/Berbers for the opposition were both available.

Enemy army is 37 Camel Riders out of ~61 units — camel cavalry was not the mainstay of Andalusi or Almoravid armies in Valencia; Berber light cavalry/knights and infantry would be far closer and are all in the engine.

The historical turning points are absent: no Almenar (1082), no capture of Berenguer Ramon II at Tevar (1090), no two-year blockade of Valencia (1093-94). Instead the middle acts are generic filler — an 'Ambush Leader', an unnamed 'Traitor', an 'Enemy Warlord' taunt, a rescue side-quest.
TREE_PALM_FOREST used as the dominant vegetation (18 objects) reads as a Saharan/Levantine desert rather than the Ebro valley and Valencian huerta.

Defeat condition on a generic KNIGHT labelled only 'Key Ally Dies' — Minaya Alvar Fanez is named in dialogue but the death condition is not identified with him, so it encodes an arbitrary unit-preservation rule.
Valencia is described as 'breached' and stormed; in fact El Cid took it after a long starvation blockade and a negotiated surrender in June 1094.
